newsitem.title: UK: AB Ports unveils Southampton terminal plan.
newsitem.headline: AB Ports unveils Southampton terminal plan.

text.p: Associated British Ports Holdings Plc revealed on Wednesday major plans to expand its main UK south coast port of Southampton.

ABP said in a statement: "The proposals -- which include berths for five new deep-sea container ships and feeder vessels -- are designed to meet the predicted national shortfall in container berths in the next century."
The UK ports group said it would develop the outline proposals with a group representing communities, residents, business and local authorities and environmentalists.

Development of the project, which will be able to handle the world's largest ships carrying in excess of 6,000 containers, will be phased in with construction starting early in the next century, ABP said.
Southampton handles 34 million tonnes of cargo a year and a record 800,000 containers moved through the port last year. It is the UK's second largest container port after Felixstowe.
However, Southampton now has limited room for further expansion on its current site despite opening its largest container berth six months ago.
Dibden Bay is a man-made site which has been reclaimed from the dredging of Southampton Water and has been earmarked for port development in the Hampshire County Structure Plan.
Port manager at ABP Southampton said: "With our new plans for Dibden we will be able to offer shipping lines the room for future growth that they are demanding."
The new terminal will create up to 1,500 permanent jobs with several hundred during the construction phase, the group added -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
